concepts.name: Finding explicit information: recall, skimming and scanning
concepts.description: Locating and retrieving facts and details that a text states directly; skimming for the gist and scanning for particular words, names, numbers and dates; answering recall questions briefly and accurately.

concepts.name: Inference: implied meanings and attitudes
concepts.description: Working out what a text suggests but does not state: a character's feelings, a writer's purpose, reasons and consequences, using clues in the wording and supporting the inference with evidence.

concepts.name: Meanings of words and phrases in context
concepts.description: Working out the meaning of unfamiliar or familiar words and phrases from the surrounding text, choosing the meaning that fits the context, and giving a one-word or short-phrase equivalent.

concepts.name: Answering in your own words (paraphrasing)
concepts.description: Re-expressing ideas from a passage in your own words without changing the meaning: replacing key words with synonyms, restructuring sentences, and avoiding lifting.

concepts.name: Writers' effects: language, imagery and structure
concepts.description: How writers achieve effects and influence readers: word choice and connotation, imagery and figurative language, sound, sentence length and structure; explaining the effect of a chosen word or phrase in context.

concepts.name: Tone, mood and the writer's attitude
concepts.description: Identifying the tone of a text or speaker (for example ironic, nostalgic, critical, urgent), the mood it creates and the writer's attitude to the subject, with evidence from the wording.

concepts.name: Facts, opinions, arguments and bias
concepts.description: Distinguishing facts from opinions; following the development of an argument; telling main points from examples and qualifying details; recognising persuasive techniques, bias and stereotyping; evaluating how convincing a text is.

concepts.name: Following ideas: reference words and linking devices
concepts.description: How ideas in a text connect: what pronouns and other reference words refer to, and what linking words signal (addition, contrast, cause and effect, time, example).

concepts.name: Making notes from a text
concepts.description: Selecting the details a task asks for and recording them as brief notes under headings, without unnecessary words; completing a set of notes from an article.

concepts.name: Reading several texts for specific information
concepts.description: Reading a set of short texts or sections (for example four or five people's accounts) and deciding which one contains a given piece of information or opinion, including paraphrased ideas.

concepts.name: Extended response to reading
concepts.description: Writing in role (as a character or participant) in a letter, report, journal, speech, interview or article, using, developing and interpreting ideas from a reading text.

concepts.name: Reading fiction: character, setting, plot, theme and style
concepts.description: Reading stories and novels for enjoyment and analysis: major and minor characters, setting in place and time, plot and conflict, themes and the writer's style; writing about a book you have read.

concepts.name: Reference sources and the parts of a book
concepts.description: Using dictionaries, thesauruses, encyclopaedias, catalogues, journals and the internet responsibly; the parts of a book (title page, contents, preface, index, glossary, appendices) and their purposes.

concepts.name: Selecting points for a summary
concepts.description: Reading the summary question carefully, identifying only the points that answer it, and separating relevant points from examples, repetition and irrelevant detail.

concepts.name: Writing a summary in continuous prose
concepts.description: Turning selected points into a concise paragraph of continuous prose in your own words, within the word limit, linking the points logically.

concepts.name: Planning and paragraphing a composition
concepts.description: Analysing a composition title, planning, writing an introduction, unified paragraphs with topic sentences, linking devices for coherence, and a conclusion; varying sentence types.

concepts.name: Narrative writing
concepts.description: Writing a story: a clear plot with conflict and resolution, a consistent point of view, convincing characters and dialogue, pace, suspense, flashback and an effective ending.

concepts.name: Descriptive writing
concepts.description: Describing a person, place, scene, event or process vividly: sensory detail, precise vocabulary, imagery, a clear structure (spatial, chronological or zoom) and atmosphere.

concepts.name: Argumentative and persuasive writing
concepts.description: Taking and defending a position on an issue: a clear stance, reasons supported by evidence and examples, counter-arguments and rebuttal, persuasive devices and a firm conclusion.

concepts.name: Discursive writing
concepts.description: Discussing an issue from several sides in a balanced way: presenting different viewpoints fairly, weighing them and reaching a reasoned conclusion.

concepts.name: Informative and expository writing
concepts.description: Explaining a topic or process clearly to inform the reader: accurate information, logical order, clear explanation and a neutral tone.

concepts.name: Register, audience and purpose
concepts.description: Choosing language suited to the audience, purpose and situation: formal, informal and semi-formal registers, tone, and the conventions of different text types.

concepts.name: Formal letters
concepts.description: The layout and language of formal letters (application, complaint, request, enquiry, letter to the editor): addresses, date, salutation, subject line, paragraphs with a clear purpose, polite firm tone, correct closing.

concepts.name: Informal letters and emails
concepts.description: Writing friendly letters and emails to friends and relatives: appropriate greetings and endings, a conversational but correct style, and covering every point the task asks for.

concepts.name: Reports
concepts.description: Writing reports for a head, a club or an organisation: a title and recipient, purpose, findings under headings, and conclusions or recommendations in an objective style.

concepts.name: Speeches
concepts.description: Writing a speech for a given occasion and audience: an engaging opening, addressing the audience, clear points, rhetorical devices and a memorable ending.

concepts.name: Articles
concepts.description: Writing articles for a school magazine or newspaper: an eye-catching headline, an engaging introduction, informative paragraphs, a lively but appropriate tone and a conclusion.

concepts.name: Memoranda (memos)
concepts.description: The format and style of an internal memo: To, From, Date, Subject, a brief purpose, numbered points or short paragraphs and a clear action required.

concepts.name: Curriculum vitae and forms
concepts.description: Compiling a curriculum vitae (personal details, education, skills, experience, referees) and completing forms accurately following the instructions.

concepts.name: Reviews
concepts.description: Writing a review of a film, book, event, restaurant or place for a general audience: describing it and giving and justifying opinions and a recommendation.

concepts.name: Journal entries and interviews
concepts.description: Writing a journal (diary) entry that reflects on events and feelings in the first person, and writing an interview as questions and answers in role.

concepts.name: Directed writing from texts
concepts.description: Using, developing and evaluating the ideas in one or two texts to write a discursive, argumentative or persuasive speech, letter, article or report for a given audience.

concepts.name: Writing from notes, graphs and statistics
concepts.description: Amplifying notes (pegs) into full sentences and paragraphs, and turning information in tables, graphs, statistics and pictures into continuous writing in a given format.

concepts.name: Nouns
concepts.description: Types of nouns (common, proper, collective, abstract, countable and uncountable), regular and irregular plurals, gender nouns, and noun formation.

concepts.name: Pronouns
concepts.description: Personal, possessive, reflexive, relative, demonstrative and indefinite pronouns; choosing the correct case (I/me, who/whom) and making pronouns agree with what they refer to.

concepts.name: Verb tenses and the sequence of tenses
concepts.description: Forming and using the present, past and future tenses in their simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous forms; irregular verbs; keeping tenses consistent (sequence of tenses).

concepts.name: Subject-verb agreement
concepts.description: Making verbs agree with their subjects, including collective nouns, 'either/neither... or/nor', 'each/every', indefinite pronouns, and subjects separated from their verbs.

concepts.name: Conditional sentences
concepts.description: Zero, first, second and third conditionals and mixed conditionals; unless, provided that, if only and I wish.

concepts.name: Auxiliary and modal verbs
concepts.description: The auxiliaries be, have and do; modal verbs (can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, would, ought to, need, dare) for ability, permission, possibility, obligation and advice.

concepts.name: Phrasal verbs
concepts.description: Verbs combined with particles (give up, put off, look after, break down, carry out): their meanings in context and their formal equivalents.

concepts.name: Active and passive voice
concepts.description: Changing sentences between the active and passive voice in all common tenses and with modals, and choosing the voice that suits the purpose.

concepts.name: Adjectives
concepts.description: Forming adjectives; comparative and superlative forms (regular and irregular); the order of adjectives before a noun; non-gradable adjectives; participial adjectives (bored/boring).

concepts.name: Adverbs and adverbials
concepts.description: Forming adverbs; adverbs and adverbial phrases of manner, time, place, frequency, degree and reason; adverbial clauses; position of adverbs.

concepts.name: Articles and determiners
concepts.description: Using a, an, the and no article; determiners such as some, any, much, many, few, a few, little, a little, each, every, either, neither.

concepts.name: Prepositions
concepts.description: Prepositions of time, place and movement, and fixed combinations of verbs, adjectives and nouns with prepositions (interested in, different from, on account of).

concepts.name: Conjunctions and discourse markers
concepts.description: Co-ordinating and subordinating conjunctions; correlative pairs; discourse markers and sentence modifiers (however, therefore, moreover, in spite of) and joining sentences with them.

concepts.name: Sentences, clauses and phrases
concepts.description: Simple, compound and complex sentences; main and subordinate clauses (noun, adjectival/relative and adverbial); phrases; combining and transforming sentences without changing the meaning.

concepts.name: Questions, question tags, commands and exclamations
concepts.description: Forming yes/no and wh- questions, indirect questions, question tags, commands and exclamations, with correct word order and punctuation.

concepts.name: Direct and indirect (reported) speech
concepts.description: Punctuating direct speech, and changing statements, questions and commands into reported speech (tense back-shift and changes to pronouns and time and place words), and back again.

concepts.name: Punctuation
concepts.description: Full stops, capital letters, commas, question and exclamation marks, apostrophes, colons, semicolons, dashes, brackets and quotation marks, and how punctuation changes meaning.

concepts.name: Word formation: prefixes and suffixes
concepts.description: Forming words with prefixes and suffixes; forming nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs from a root word; using the correct form of a word in a sentence.

concepts.name: Homonyms, homophones, homographs and confusable words
concepts.description: Words that sound or look alike but differ in meaning (their/there/they're, stationary/stationery, principal/principle, affect/effect, lead/lead) and choosing the right one.

concepts.name: Synonyms and antonyms
concepts.description: Words with similar and opposite meanings; choosing the most precise synonym for a context; forming opposites with prefixes.

concepts.name: Idioms, proverbs and collocations
concepts.description: Common English idioms and proverbs and their meanings, and collocations (words that usually go together, such as make a decision, heavy rain, strong tea).

concepts.name: Spelling
concepts.description: Spelling rules (i before e, doubling final consonants, dropping silent e, y to i, -ful, plurals) and commonly misspelt words.

concepts.name: Figures of speech
concepts.description: Recognising and using simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole, alliteration, onomatopoeia, irony, oxymoron, euphemism, rhetorical question and repetition, and their effects.

concepts.name: Listening skills
concepts.description: Listening for gist and detail, following directions and instructions, taking notes and messages from talks, announcements and conversations, and recognising speakers' attitudes.

concepts.name: Pronunciation, stress and intonation
concepts.description: English vowel and consonant sounds, diphthongs, silent letters, word stress (including stress that changes a noun into a verb), sentence stress and rising and falling intonation.

concepts.name: Conversations, telephone calls and interviews
concepts.description: Polite and appropriate spoken English for greetings, introductions, requests, invitations, apologies, complaints, condolences, telephone calls, conversations and interviews.

concepts.name: Talks, speeches and debates
concepts.description: Preparing and giving a short talk or speech, impromptu speaking, and debating: structuring points, supporting them, using discourse markers, and responding to others.
